title: Custom In-Memory Security/Authorization Rules
pattern: Parsing authorization rules, access control lists, and user scopes dynamically using string concatenation and matching inside application loops.
why_bad: It bypasses compiler guarantees for access paths, leading to potential security vulnerabilities due to minor typos. It makes security audits hard because the roles are handled as opaque string arrays.
detection: String manipulation and comparison loops evaluated to establish authorization bounds in domain code.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Dynamic systems where roles, scopes, and target rules are updated in database records by security administrators.
source: Heather Adkins_ Betsy Beyer_ Paul Blankinship_ Ana Oprea_ Piotr - _Building Secure and Reliable Systems_ Best Practices for Designing, Implementing, and Maintaining Systems_ (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 11; Vaughn Vernon - _Implementing Domain-Driven Design_ (2013, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Chapter 3.
